entries.corrected: proved / unresolved (exclusive, sums to 100%)

entries.claim: time at which each arm first met the requested tolerance
entries.corrected: NOT INSTRUMENTED in protocol v1; wall_s is a stopping time and for a timed-out record equals the budget
entries.note: log (t, L, U, status) at every bound update; derive first-attainment and anytime AUC from that stream.

entries.claim: no bound inversion occurs
entries.corrected: 12 negative gaps in policy_pilot, min -1.137e-13, not clipped
entries.note: roundoff-scale bound inversion (order 1e-13) in every policy-pilot arm including the unconditional baseline, so it is a property of the shared float bound evaluation, not of conditioning. Consistent with float_unverified status; it is recorded rather than clipped, and an enclosed implementation (P4) must make it impossible.

entries.claim: n = 330 per arm
entries.corrected: 360 cells - 30 void = 330 x 5 arms = 1650 records
entries.note: 291 timeouts are (cell, arm) records out of 1650, not 291 of the 330 cells

entries.claim: model-effect intervals validated and classified
entries.corrected: 75 validated by enumeration (0 failures) AND 40 classified on pilot instances -- disjoint populations
entries.note: no interval is unaccounted for; the two totals answer different questions and must not appear in one row

entries.claim: fraction of candidate comparisons the certificate resolves
entries.corrected: 60/66 = 90.9% (unordered, matched)
entries.note: l_i <= u_i for every candidate, so u_i < l_j and u_j < l_i cannot both hold. Each resolved inequality therefore identifies a distinct unordered pair, and the matched denominator is k(k-1)/2.

entries.claim: certifiability is cheap because G3 passed
entries.corrected: PASS is arithmetically correct but uninformative
entries.note: the constrained arm is A+B (mean 0.4573), not the best available certifiable model A (mean 0.7253). The gate never compared the free model against the strongest constrained one, and it passes because the free arm scored 0.1212.

entries.claim: what the trained predictor arms consumed as graph input
entries.corrected: the guide's own 21-mer MFE structure; no target window
entries.note: these arms fold the assayed guide's OWN sequence, so no native transcript was substituted for a reporter construct (unlike F9). They are a valid optimisation diagnostic and cannot support any target-structure claim.

entries.claim: the predictor split supports a generalisation claim
entries.corrected: one held-out gene (['UBE2D3']), test n=69
entries.note: one held-out gene; not a population claim

entries.claim: the additive anchor is non-negative
entries.corrected: signed: nn.Linear with unconstrained weight and bias
entries.note: the non-negativity constraint belongs to certmp's monotone MPNN (phase one), not to scmp's anchor. The report's limits table carried the phase-one restriction across to phase two. This matters: a signed anchor is strictly more expressive and does not obstruct the support oracle, which optimises a linear objective over the family regardless of coefficient sign.

entries.claim: sum+ReLU with non-negative parameters is additive in the graph z
entries.corrected: f(z) = 2z1 + 2z2 + 2z1z2 on the three-node path; mixed difference 2 with every ReLU stable
entries.note: C4 varied X with the adjacency fixed, establishing affinity in X only. Additivity in z is a different statement and is false.

entries.claim: the residual g is non-additive in z on a real feasible family
entries.corrected: relative residual 2.365e-02 after projecting 20 enumerated members onto [1, z]
entries.note: capacity for non-additive structure is present. This is NOT evidence that it generalises: G4 measured generalisation and failed.

entries.claim: layer 1 needs no relaxation at all
entries.corrected: message M1 exactly affine; its ReLU relaxed, 2 unstable units observed
entries.note: the implementation was already correct; the report's sentence generalised a true statement about the message to the whole layer

entries.claim: kappa_L bounds the relaxation ratio for arbitrary positive features
entries.note: the uniform-feature identity is untouched; only its feature-independent extension is refuted

entries.claim: the relaxation-gap exponent 0.912 per layer is architectural
entries.corrected: kappa_L = (2m-1)^L without self-loops, m^L with them: the exponent depends on the family and the self-loop convention
entries.note: C5's measurement stands on the family C5 used; the universal reading does not

entries.claim: the closed-form kappa applies to the implemented model
entries.reported: kappa_L presented without stating the fixed part B
entries.corrected: B = I + chain at every call site; kappa is no clean power (m=3,L=2 gives 177/41 vs 9 for self-loops only)
entries.note: B = I + chain is present in every member, so the union and the maximum share a fixed core and the ratio is compressed toward 1 relative to the candidate-only formulas. Any kappa quoted for this model must be derived under B, not borrowed from the matching closed form.

entries.claim: G4 tested the anchor+residual decomposition
entries.corrected: candidates=(), so a^T z == 0 and P z == 0 in every predictor arm
entries.note: run_pilot builds CertifiedModel(d_in, tuple(), ...) with an EMPTY candidate set and passes an empty z, so a^T z is identically zero and P z is zero. G4 did not test the anchor+residual decomposition over any family.

entries.claim: the weak arm underfits or is buggy

entries.note: a generalisation failure, not an optimisation failure; the diagnosis comes from the training curve, not the test score

entries.claim: A-initialised residual training beats the old setup
entries.reported: old setup: residual on gamma=1 from scratch
entries.corrected: A_init_finetune delta -0.7329 vs A_only on 5/5 seeds; old setup +0.3714 on 0/5
entries.note: synthetic, one family, size holdout; a mechanism result, not a predictive one

entries.claim: the residual carries useful nonlinear predictive value
entries.corrected: a pairwise ridge is EXACT (MSE 0.0000) on path_matching|interacting where A_init_residual is 10.3087; no benefit at all on layered_dag
entries.note: the residual learns ~8% of the target projection residual and ~13% of its mixed-difference magnitude: real but far short. NOTE the targets are exactly linear in an explicit basis, which favours ridge by construction; a fair retest needs non-basis-representable targets

entries.claim: the residual avoids harm on deliberately additive targets
